newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares continue to climb toward new heights.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares continue to climb toward new heights.

text.p: Danish share prices continued to climb on Friday, powered mainly by buoyant A.P. Moeller and Thursday's Wall Street surge.
By 1115 GMT the KFX top-20 index had gained 1.80 point -- 1.09 percent -- to stand at 167.65 and its June future was up 2.15 point to 167.15.

Shipping group Moeller's D/S 1912 rose 7,000 crowns to 241,000 and sister D/S Svendborg was up 13,667 crowns, to 343,000. They were continuing a rise begun Thursday in the wake of strong first quarter results from Norwegian shipping heavyweight Bergesen.
Sophus Berendsen contributed to the overall climb with a rise of 17 crowns, to 890.

But the big banks, which had been expected to be in the vanguard of advances, were mainly static, with Den Danske Bank unchanged at 620 crowns and Unidanmark stationary at 353 crowns. Third-largest bank BG Bank rose a single crown, to 315.00. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
